See docs/01-app/02-guides/instant-navigation.mdx */} 14 15 > This page covers caching with [Cache Components](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents), enabled by setting [`cacheComponents: true`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) in your `next.config.ts` file. If you're not using Cache Components, see the [Caching and Revalidating (Previous Model)](/docs/app/guides/caching-without-cache-components) guide. 16 17 Caching is a technique for storing the result of data fetching and other computations so that future requests for the same data can be served faster, without doing the work again. 18 19 ## Enabling Cache Components 20 21 You can enable Cache Components by adding the [`cacheComponents`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) option to your Next config file: 22 23 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" highlight={4} switcher 24 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 25 26 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 27 cacheComponents: true, 28 } 29 30 export default nextConfig 31 ``` 32 33 ```js filename="next.config.js" highlight={3} switcher 34 /** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */ 35 const nextConfig = { 36 cacheComponents: true, 37 } 38 39 module.exports = nextConfig 40 ``` 41 42 > **Good to know:** When Cache Components is enabled, `GET` Route Handlers follow the same prerendering model as pages. See [Route Handlers with Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/route-handlers#with-cache-components) for details. 43 44 ## Usage 45 46 The [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) directive caches the return value of async functions and components. You can apply it at two levels: 47 48 - **Data-level**: Cache a function that fetches or computes data (e.g., `getProducts()`, `getUser(id)`) 49 - **UI-level**: Cache an entire component or page (e.g., `async function BlogPosts()`) 50 51 > Arguments and any closed-over values from parent scopes automatically become part of the [cache key](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache#cache-keys), which means different inputs will produce separate cache entries. This enables personalized or parameterized cached content. See [serialization requirements and constraints](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache#constraints) for details on what can be cached and how arguments work. 52 53 ### Data-level caching 54 55 To cache an asynchronous function that fetches data, add the `use cache` directive at the top of the function body: 56 57 ```tsx filename="app/lib/data.ts" highlight={3,4,5} 58 import { cacheLife } from 'next/cache' 59 60 export async function getUsers() { 61 'use cache' 62 cacheLife('hours') 63 return db.query('SELECT * FROM users') 64 } 65 ``` 66 67 Data-level caching is useful when the same data is used across multiple components, or when you want to cache the data independently from the UI. 68 69 ### UI-level caching 70 71 To cache an entire component, page, or layout, add the `use cache` directive at the top of the component or page body: 72 73 ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" highlight={1,4,5} 74 import { cacheLife } from 'next/cache' 75 76 export default async function Page() { 77 'use cache' 78 cacheLife('hours') 79 80 const users = await db.query('SELECT * FROM users') 81 82 return ( 83
    84 {users.map((user) => ( 85
  • {user.name}
    • 86 ))} 87
88 ) 89 } 90 ``` 91 92 > If you add "`use cache`" at the top of a file, all exported functions in the file will be cached. 93 94 ### Streaming uncached data 95 96 For components that fetch data from an asynchronous source such as an API, a database, or any other async operation, and require fresh data on every request, do not use `"use cache"`. 97 98 Instead, wrap the component in [``](https://react.dev/reference/react/Suspense) and provide a fallback UI. At request time, React renders the fallback first, then streams in the resolved content once the async work completes. 99 100 ```tsx filename="page.tsx" 101 import { Suspense } from 'react' 102 103 async function LatestPosts() { 104 const data = await fetch('https://api.example.com/posts') 105 const posts = await data.json() 106 return ( 107
    108 {posts.map((post) => ( 109
  • {post.title}

112 ) 113 } 114 115 export default function Page() { 116 return ( 117 <> 118

Loading posts...

`) is included in the static shell, while the component's content streams in at request time. 128 129 `` provides a fallback UI while async work completes, but it does not itself opt a component into dynamic rendering. If a component only performs synchronous work, it will complete during prerendering regardless of whether it is wrapped in ``. 130 131 ## Working with runtime APIs 132 133 Runtime APIs require information that is only available when a user makes a request. These include: 134 135 - [`cookies`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cookies) - User's cookie data 136 - [`headers`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/headers) - Request headers 137 - [`searchParams`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page#searchparams-optional) - URL query parameters 138 - [`params`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page#params-optional) - Dynamic route parameters (unless at least one sample is provided via [`generateStaticParams`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-static-params)). 139 140 Components that access runtime APIs should be wrapped in ``: 141 142 ```tsx filename="page.tsx" 143 import { cookies } from 'next/headers' 144 import { Suspense } from 'react' 145 146 async function UserGreeting() { 147 const cookieStore = await cookies() 148 const theme = cookieStore.get('theme')?.value || 'light' 149 return

Your theme: {theme}

150 } 151 152 export default function Page() { 153 return ( 154 <> 155

Dashboard

156 Loading...

}> 157 158 159 160 ) 161 } 162 ``` 163 164 ### Passing runtime values to cached functions 165 166 You can extract values from runtime APIs and pass them as arguments to cached functions: 167 168 ```tsx filename="app/profile/page.tsx" 169 import { cookies } from 'next/headers' 170 import { Suspense } from 'react' 171 172 export default function Page() { 173 return ( 174 Loading...}> 175 176 177 ) 178 } 179 180 // Component (not cached) reads runtime data 181 async function ProfileContent() { 182 const session = (await cookies()).get('session')?.value 183 return 184 } 185 186 // Cached component receives extracted value as a prop 187 async function CachedContent({ sessionId }: { sessionId: string }) { 188 'use cache' 189 // sessionId becomes part of the cache key 190 const data = await fetchUserData(sessionId) 191 return
{data}
192 } 193 ``` 194 195 At request time, `CachedContent` executes if no matching cache entry is found, and stores the result for future requests with the same `sessionId`. 196 197 By default, `use cache` stores entries [in-memory](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache#runtime-caching-considerations). In serverless environments where memory doesn't persist across requests, `CachedContent` may re-evaluate on every request. Consider [`'use cache: remote'`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache-remote) for durable, shared caching. 198 199 ## Working with non-deterministic operations 200 201 Operations like `Math.random()`, `Date.now()`, or `crypto.randomUUID()` produce different values each time they execute. Cache Components requires you to explicitly handle these. 202 203 **To generate unique values per request**, defer to request time by calling [`connection()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/connection) before these operations, and wrap the component in ``: 204 205 ```tsx filename="page.tsx" 206 import { connection } from 'next/server' 207 import { Suspense } from 'react' 208 209 async function UniqueContent() { 210 await connection() 211 const uuid = crypto.randomUUID() 212 return

Request ID: {uuid}

213 } 214 215 export default function Page() { 216 return ( 217 Loading...

}> 218 219 220 ) 221 } 222 ``` 223 224 Alternatively, you can **cache the result** so all users see the same value until revalidation: 225 226 ```tsx filename="page.tsx" 227 export default async function Page() { 228 'use cache' 229 const buildId = crypto.randomUUID() 230 return

Build ID: {buildId}

231 } 232 ``` 233 234 ## Working with deterministic operations 235 236 Operations like synchronous I/O, module imports, and pure computations can complete during prerendering. Components using only these operations have their rendered output automatically included in the static HTML shell. 237 238 ```tsx filename="page.tsx" 239 import fs from 'node:fs' 240 241 export default async function Page() { 242 const content = fs.readFileSync('./config.json', 'utf-8') 243 const constants = await import('./constants.json') 244 const processed = JSON.parse(content).items.map((item) => item.value * 2) 245 246 return ( 247
248

{constants.appName}

  • {value}
    • 252 ))} 253
254
255 ) 256 } 257 ``` 258 259 > **Good to know:** This includes queries to embedded databases with synchronous APIs, such as `better-sqlite3` or Node.js's built-in [`node:sqlite`](https://nodejs.org/api/sqlite.html). If you need per-request data from a synchronous source, call [`connection()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/connection) before the query. 260 261 ## How rendering works 262 263 At build time, Next.js renders your route's component tree. How each component is handled depends on the APIs it uses: 264 265 - [`use cache`](#usage): the result is cached and included in the static shell 266 - [``](#streaming-uncached-data): fallback UI is included in the static shell while the content streams at request time 267 - [Deterministic operations](#working-with-deterministic-operations): like pure computations and module imports are automatically included in the static shell 268 269 This generates a static shell consisting of HTML for initial page loads and a serialized [RSC Payload](/docs/app/getting-started/server-and-client-components#on-the-server) for client-side navigation, ensuring the browser receives fully rendered content instantly whether users navigate directly to the URL or transition from another page. 270 271 278 279 This rendering approach is called **Partial Prerendering (PPR)**, and it's the default behavior with Cache Components. 280 281 > You can verify that a route was fully prerendered by checking the [build output summary](/docs/app/api-reference/cli/next#next-build-options). Alternatively, see what content was added to the static shell of any page by viewing the page source in your browser. 282 283 290 291 Next.js requires you to explicitly handle components that can't complete during prerendering. If they aren't wrapped in `` or marked with `use cache`, you'll see an [`Uncached data was accessed outside of `](https://nextjs.org/docs/messages/blocking-route) error during development and build time. 292 293 > **🎥 Watch:** Why Partial Prerendering and how it works → [YouTube (10 minutes)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MTcPrTIBkpA). 294 295 ### Opting out of the static shell 296 297 Placing a `` boundary with an empty fallback above the document body in your Root Layout causes the entire app to defer to request time. Because the fallback is empty, there is no static shell to send immediately, so every request blocks until the page is fully rendered. To limit this to specific routes, use [multiple root layouts](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/layout#root-layout). 298 299 ```tsx filename="app/layout.tsx" highlight={1,10-12} 300 import { Suspense } from 'react' 301 302 export default function RootLayout({ 303 children, 304 }: { 305 children: React.ReactNode 306 }) { 307 return ( 308 309 310 {children} 311 312 313 ) 314 } 315 ``` 316 317 > **Good to know**: This same pattern applies when `generateViewport` accesses uncached dynamic data. See [Viewport with Cache Components](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-viewport#with-cache-components) for a detailed example. 318 319 ### Putting it all together 320 321 Here's a complete example showing static content, cached dynamic content, and streaming dynamic content working together on a single page: 322 323 ```tsx filename="app/blog/page.tsx" 324 import { Suspense } from 'react' 325 import { cookies } from 'next/headers' 326 import { cacheLife, cacheTag, updateTag } from 'next/cache' 327 import Link from 'next/link' 328 329 export default function BlogPage() { 330 return ( 331 <> 332 {/* Static content - prerendered automatically */} 333
334

Our Blog

335
336 Home | About 337
338
339 340 {/* Cached dynamic content - included in the static shell */} 341 342 343 {/* Runtime dynamic content - streams at request time */} 344 Loading your preferences...

}> 345 346 347 348 {/* Mutation - server action that revalidates the cache */} 349 Loading...

}> 350 351 352 353 ) 354 } 355 356 // Everyone sees the same blog posts (revalidated every hour) 357 async function BlogPosts() { 358 'use cache' 359 cacheLife('hours') 360 cacheTag('posts') 361 362 const res = await fetch('https://api.vercel.app/blog') 363 const posts = await res.json() 364 365 return ( 366
367

Latest Posts

1 --- 2 title: cacheLife 3 description: Learn how to use the cacheLife function to set the cache expiration time for a cached function or component. 4 related: 5 title: Related 6 description: View related API references. 7 links: 8 - app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents 9 - app/api-reference/directives/use-cache 10 - app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag 11 - app/api-reference/functions/cacheTag 12 --- 13 14 The `cacheLife` function is used to set the cache lifetime of a function or component. It should be used alongside the [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) directive, and within the scope of the function or component. 15 16 ## Usage 17 18 ### Basic setup 19 20 To use `cacheLife`, first enable the [`cacheComponents` flag](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) in your `next.config.js` file: 21 22 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher 23 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 24 25 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 26 cacheComponents: true, 27 } 28 29 export default nextConfig 30 ``` 31 32 ```js filename="next.config.js" switcher 33 const nextConfig = { 34 cacheComponents: true, 35 } 36 37 export default nextConfig 38 ``` 39 40 `cacheLife` can only be used within a cache directive scope. 41 42 Add a cache directive (for example, `use cache`) at the file level or at the top of an async function or component. 43 44 `cacheLife` cannot be used at module scope. Calling it at the top level of a file will throw an error. 45 46 > **Good to know**: 47 > 48 > - Calling `cacheLife` is optional. If omitted, a default cache lifetime is applied. 49 > - Call `cacheLife` in the same function or component where caching is defined. Avoid abstracting it into shared utilities so the cache behavior remains explicit and easy to reason about. 50 > - If you call `cacheLife`, ensure only one call executes per function invocation. You can call it in different control flow branches, but only one should run per request. See the [conditional cache lifetimes](#conditional-cache-lifetimes) example. 51 52 ### Using preset profiles 53 54 Next.js provides preset cache profiles that cover common caching needs. Each profile balances three factors: 55 56 - How long users see cached content without checking for updates (client-side) 57 - How often fresh content is generated on the server 58 - When old content expires completely 59 60 Choose a profile based on how frequently your content changes: 61 62 - **`seconds`** - Real-time data (stock prices, live scores) 63 - **`minutes`** - Frequently updated (social feeds, news) 64 - **`hours`** - Multiple daily updates (product inventory, weather) 65 - **`days`** - Daily updates (blog posts, articles) 66 - **`weeks`** - Weekly updates (podcasts, newsletters) 67 - **`max`** - Rarely changes (legal pages, archived content) 68 69 Import `cacheLife` and pass a profile name: 70 71 ```tsx filename="app/blog/page.tsx" highlight={1,5} 72 'use cache' 73 import { cacheLife } from 'next/cache' 74 75 export default async function BlogPage() { 76 cacheLife('days') // Blog content updated daily 77 78 const posts = await getBlogPosts() 79 return
{/* render posts */}
80 } 81 ``` 82 83 The profile name tells Next.js how to cache the entire function's output. If you don't call `cacheLife`, the `default` profile is used. See [preset cache profiles](#preset-cache-profiles) for timing details. 84 85 ## Reference 86 87 ### Cache profile properties 88 89 Cache profiles control caching behavior through three timing properties: 90 91 - **[`stale`](#stale)**: How long the client can use cached data without checking the server 92 - **[`revalidate`](#revalidate)**: After this time, the next request will trigger a background refresh 93 - **[`expire`](#expire)**: After this time with no requests, the next one waits for fresh content 94 95 #### `stale` 96 97 **Client-side:** How long the client can use cached data without checking the server. 98 99 During this time, the client-side router displays cached content immediately without any network request. After this period expires, the router must check with the server on the next navigation or request. This provides instant page loads from the client cache, but data may be outdated. 100 101 - If omitted, defaults to the `default` profile's `stale` value (5 minutes, see [`staleTimes`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/staleTimes)) 102 103 ```tsx 104 cacheLife({ stale: 300 }) // 5 minutes 105 ``` 106 107 #### `revalidate` 108 109 How often the server regenerates cached content in the background. 110 111 - When a request arrives after this period, the server: 112 1. Serves the cached version immediately (if available) 113 2. Regenerates content in the background 114 3. Updates the cache with fresh content 115 - Similar to [Incremental Static Regeneration (ISR)](/docs/app/guides/incremental-static-regeneration) 116 - If omitted, defaults to the `default` profile's `revalidate` value (15 minutes) 117 118 ```tsx 119 cacheLife({ revalidate: 900 }) // 15 minutes 120 ``` 121 122 #### `expire` 123 124 Maximum time before the server must regenerate cached content. 125 126 - After this period with no traffic, the server regenerates content synchronously on the next request 127 - When you set both `revalidate` and `expire`, `expire` must be longer than `revalidate`. Next.js validates this and raises an error for invalid configurations. 128 - If omitted, defaults to the `default` profile's `expire` value (never expires) 129 130 ```tsx 131 cacheLife({ expire: 3600 }) // 1 hour 132 ``` 133 134 ### Preset cache profiles 135 136 If you don't specify a profile, Next.js uses the `default` profile. We recommend explicitly setting a profile to make caching behavior clear. 137 138 | **Profile** | **Use Case** | `stale` | `revalidate` | `expire` | 139 | ----------- | -------------------------------------- | ---------- | ------------ | -------- | 140 | `default` | Standard content | 5 minutes | 15 minutes | never | 141 | `seconds` | Real-time data | 30 seconds | 1 second | 1 minute | 142 | `minutes` | Frequently updated content | 5 minutes | 1 minute | 1 hour | 143 | `hours` | Content updated multiple times per day | 5 minutes | 1 hour | 1 day | 144 | `days` | Content updated daily | 5 minutes | 1 day | 1 week | 145 | `weeks` | Content updated weekly | 5 minutes | 1 week | 30 days | 146 | `max` | Stable content that rarely changes | 5 minutes | 30 days | 1 year | 147 148 ### Custom cache profiles 149 150 Define reusable cache profiles in your `next.config.ts` file: 151 152 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" 153 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 154 155 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 156 cacheComponents: true, 157 cacheLife: { 158 biweekly: { 159 stale: 60 * 60 * 24 * 14, // 14 days 160 revalidate: 60 * 60 * 24, // 1 day 161 expire: 60 * 60 * 24 * 14, // 14 days 162 }, 163 }, 164 } 165 166 export default nextConfig 167 ``` 168 169 ```js filename="next.config.js" switcher 170 const nextConfig = { 171 cacheComponents: true, 172 cacheLife: { 173 biweekly: { 174 stale: 60 * 60 * 24 * 14, // 14 days 175 revalidate: 60 * 60 * 24, // 1 day 176 expire: 60 * 60 * 24 * 14, // 14 days 177 }, 178 }, 179 } 180 181 module.exports = nextConfig 182 ``` 183 184 The example above caches for 14 days, checks for updates daily, and expires the cache after 14 days. You can then reference this profile throughout your application by its name: 185 186 > **Good to know**: Any omitted properties in a custom profile inherit from the `default` profile. This also applies to inline profile objects passed directly to `cacheLife()`. 187 188 ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" highlight={5} 189 'use cache' 190 import { cacheLife } from 'next/cache' 191 192 export default async function Page() { 193 cacheLife('biweekly') 194 return
Page

Add a cache directive (for example, `use cache`) at the file level or at the top of an async function or component. `cacheLife` cannot be used at module scope. Calling it at the top level of a file will throw an error. > **Good to know**: > > - Calling `cacheLife` is optional. If omitted, a default cache lifetime is applied. > - Call `cacheLife` in the same function or component where caching is defined. Avoid abstracting it into shared utilities so the cache behavior remains explicit and easy to reason about. > - If you call `cacheLife`, ensure only one call executes per function invocation. You can call it in different control flow branches, but only one should run per request. See the [conditional cache lifetimes](#conditional-cache-lifetimes) example. ### Using preset profiles Next.js provides preset cache profiles that cover common caching needs. Each profile balances three factors: - How long users see cached content without checking for updates (client-side) - How often fresh content is generated on the server - When old content expires completely Choose a profile based on how frequently your content changes: - **`seconds`** - Real-time data (stock prices, live scores) - **`minutes`** - Frequently updated (social feeds, news) - **`hours`** - Multiple daily updates (product inventory, weather) - **`days`** - Daily updates (blog posts, articles) - **`weeks`** - Weekly updates (podcasts, newsletters) - **`max`** - Rarely changes (legal pages, archived content) Import `cacheLife` and pass a profile name: ```tsx filename="app/blog/page.tsx" highlight={1,5} 'use cache' import { cacheLife } from 'next/cache' export default async function BlogPage() { cacheLife('days') // Blog content updated daily const posts = await getBlogPosts() return
{/* render posts */}
